evidence: Traupman 215: autoraedam gubernāre, to drive a car
terms.comment: A description of ours, with Traupman’s car and his verb for driving it (see car, drive). No reference work has a word for a self-driving car. autoraeda automata would say it more briefly, but in modern Latin automatum and automatārius are used of any motor vehicle (see automaton), so the phrase would not tell the new car from the old.

phrases.latin: Hanc autoraedam nēmō gubernat; sē ipsa gubernat!
phrases.english: Nobody is driving this car; it drives itself!

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 215.
